text: Apple reports record quarterly revenue of $124 billion, up 9% year over year, and raises its dividend by 4%.
Nvidia cuts its full-year revenue outlook, citing new U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips to China.
Microsoft agrees to acquire a cybersecurity start-up for $8 billion in cash; the deal is expected to close next quarter.
Boeing announces that its chief executive will retire at year end; the board has begun a search for a successor.
The FDA approves Eli Lilly's new obesity pill after a priority review.
Johnson & Johnson is ordered by a jury to pay $2.1 billion in damages in a product liability case; the company will appeal.
The Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged and signals two cuts later this year.
U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than economists expected, led by shelter and energy.
The European Central Bank lowers its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.00%.
Exxon Mobil and Chevron shares are in focus after OPEC+ agrees to a larger-than-expected production cut.
JPMorgan Chase announces a new $30 billion share repurchase program after passing the stress test.
Tesla recalls 400,000 vehicles over a software issue affecting rear-view cameras; a free over-the-air update will fix it.
Amazon unveils a new generation of in-house AI chips for its cloud customers.
Pfizer's late-stage trial of an experimental heart drug fails to meet its main goal.
UnitedHealth discloses a cyberattack that disrupted claims processing at one of its units.
Walmart beats quarterly earnings estimates and raises its annual sales forecast.
Intel to lay off 15% of its workforce as part of a $10 billion cost-cutting plan.
The U.S. Commerce Department adds 30 Chinese entities to its export blacklist, restricting sales of semiconductor tools.
A magnitude 7.4 earthquake strikes off the coast of Taiwan; chip plants report minor disruptions.
Goldman Sachs prices $5 billion of senior notes in three tranches.
Meta Platforms is fined 1.2 billion euros by EU regulators for data transfer violations.
Netflix adds a record 19 million subscribers in the quarter, far above forecasts.
Coca-Cola names its chief operating officer as the next chief executive, effective in May.
Disney and a striking union reach a tentative agreement, ending a four-month strike.
Payrolls rose by 275,000 in February and the unemployment rate held at 3.9%.
Russia and Ukraine agree to a temporary ceasefire around key ports, easing grain export concerns.
Alphabet shares fall after the U.S. Justice Department proposes structural remedies in its search monopoly case.
Caterpillar reports a 12% drop in quarterly sales as construction demand weakens; it keeps its outlook.
Visa and Mastercard settle a long-running lawsuit with merchants over card fees.
The company will be added to the S&P 500 index effective before the open on Monday, replacing a departing member.
Oracle signs a multiyear cloud contract worth more than $30 billion a year with an undisclosed customer.
Starbucks withdraws its annual guidance amid falling store traffic in China and the U.S.
Procter & Gamble holds its quarterly dividend at $1.01 per share, in line with the previous quarter.
A fire at a refinery in Texas forces a shutdown of production units for several weeks.
The White House issues an executive order imposing a 25% tariff on imported heavy trucks.
AbbVie raises its long-term sales forecast for its immunology drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq.
Broadcom completes its acquisition of a virtualization software company after final regulatory approval.
Bank of America's chief financial officer steps down for personal reasons; an interim CFO is named.
The quarterly report on Form 10-Q is filed with no material changes to risk factors.
Costco reports October same-store sales up 6%, in line with expectations.
